- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 5–10 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after 10–15 days of high sentiment; apply mean reversion bias: if 30d avg is 78–82, forecast should not fall below 75–77 unless sentiment confirms.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage sentiment-driven corrections; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment was positive 5–7 days prior.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” (e.g., spike then sharp drop), model often misses the second drop; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for 3–7 days after peak.
